title: Review of c07 ringswim c2 (SIBM, L4b[L3]): ring and swimming both replicate on fresh seeds 5 and 6, but the aggregate ring fails 1.5 on both and the farthest swimmer carries no ring; Weak
summary: I looked at the claim's radial and tracks images, then re-ran world_claim.py with labkit on new seeds 5 and 6, world_chi0.py and world_mu0.py on seed 5, and celltrack.py on seed 5. Link ring, aggregate L rim/core (rim/outside): seed 5 1.45 (6.56), 31/49 cells membrane-like; seed 6 1.40 (6.53), 24/43; chi=0 1.13 (0/109); mu=0 (static) 1.61 (78/100). Motion: labkit max 5.9 and 4.0 body lengths; celltrack on seed 5 finds 22 track segments >= 3 BL (mu=0: labkit max 2.9 BL). But in seed 5 the labkit top tracks that are membrane-like (#5, #48, #170) are round, slow cells, while the farthest mover (#442, 5.9 BL, a large crescent at t=17600-20000) is not membrane-like (rerun/seed5/tracks.png, FACTS.md): the ring and the motion are seen in different individuals. In the last quarter of seed 5 bodies elongate into long crescents and strips spanning a third of the domain.

observations.S: rerun/seed5/sheet.png t=0: noise over the whole domain
observations.B: rerun/seed5/radial.png: L rim/core 1.45, rim/outside 6.56, 31/49 cells membrane-like (chi=0: 1.13, 0/109); seed 6: 1.40, 24/43
observations.M: rerun/seed5/FACTS.md: track 442 moves 5.9 BL; celltrack_s5.json: 22 segments >= 3 BL; mu=0: max 2.9 BL

seeds_run.result: partial: ring 1.45 (< 1.5 aggregate), motion yes, farthest swimmer not ringed

verdicts.limitation: The ring fails the 1.5 aggregate test on both fresh seeds (as on the author's seed 1), and swimming weakens it: static cells (mu=0) are ringed at 1.61. The swimmer I checked is unringed, so L4b[L3] (ringed swimmers) is not shown for the same individuals; a per-track check of rim/core for every >= 3 BL segment would settle it. The drive is a per-body label average (nonlocal). No dt or resolution check.
